text: The Gibson–Fawcett Award is presented every two years by the Royal Society of Chemistry to honor exceptional contributions in materials chemistry, with a specific focus on the originality and independence of the research.[2][3] Established in 2008, the award is administered by the Materials Chemistry Division Awards Committee and is restricted to researchers who are under 40 years of age.[4] The prize was discontinued in 2020.[5] It is named in honor of Reginald Gibson and Eric Fawcett, two prominent chemists who collaborated with Anton Michels in investigating the effects of high pressure on chemical reactions, a study that ultimately led to the discovery of polyethylene.[6]
